title: Magnetars, Soft Gamma Repeaters and Anomalous X-Ray Pulsars Against Magnetic-Field, Density and Energy Bounds

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Settle in.
paragraphs: Welcome in. I am Professor Francesca Bianchi, and this is Magnetars, Soft Gamma Repeaters and Anomalous X-Ray Pulsars Against Magnetic-Field, Density and Energy Bounds. This is lesson 1 of 1 in the full thirty-minute build of this class. In this lesson we take the class's own material in order — nothing here is imported, and nothing is asked later that is not taught here first. We begin here: Settle in.

Settle in. I am Professor Francesca Bianchi, and this is Magnetars, Soft Gamma Repeaters and Anomalous X-Ray Pulsars Against Magnetic-Field, Density and Energy Bounds. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

'Characteristic Ages Against Supernova Remnant Ages: What the Discrepancies Require of Magnetar Birth Periods and Braking Histories'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): largest_age_ratio_source = 1E 2259+586; largest_age_ratio = 16.5; smallest_age_ratio = 0.02; sources_tau_c_exceeds_remnant_by_10x = 1. These values were computed by the deposited compute.py from published values, under the assumptions stated in the paper.
Now we go one step further into the material.

'Crustal Failure Stresses in Magnetars: Surface Magnetic Stress Against the Breaking Strength of the Neutron Star Crust'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): breaking_field_theta0.01_G = 5.01e+14; breaking_field_theta0.1_G = 1.59e+15; sources_surface_stress_above_theta0.01 = 3; highest_stress_source = SGR 1806-20; highest_stress_dyn_cm2 = 1.51e+29. These values were computed by the deposited compute.py from published values, under the assumptions stated in the paper.
The next piece is where this starts to come together.

'Dipole Magnetic Fields of Eighteen Magnetars from Spin-Down: A Catalogue-Wide Recalculation Against the Quantum Critical Field'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): highest_B_source = SGR 1806-20; highest_B_G = 1.95e+15; lowest_B_source = SGR 0418+5729; lowest_B_G = 6.10e+12; median_B_G = 2.22e+14; span_in_B = 319.1; sources_above_BQ = 16; n_sources = 18. These values were computed by the deposited compute.py from published values, under the assumptions stated in the paper.
Listen carefully here — this piece carries weight in the questions later.

'Field-Decay Heating and Persistent X-Ray Luminosity: Required Decay Times for the Magnetar Catalogue'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): longest_required_decay_time_source = CXOU J164710.2-455216; longest_required_decay_time_yr = 5.28e+06; shortest_required_decay_time_yr = 3.27e+02; sources_Lx_above_Edot = 11; median_Lx_over_decay_power = 0.387. These values were computed by the deposited compute.py from published values, under the assumptions stated in the paper.
We take the pieces in order, because each one stands on the last.

'Giant Flare Energy Budgets: The Three Recorded Events Against the Magnetic Reservoir of Their Host Stars'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): largest_flare_source = SGR 1806-20; largest_flare_energy_erg = 2.0e+46; largest_flare_fraction_of_reservoir = 0.032; smallest_flare_fraction_of_reservoir = 2.45e-03; reservoir_SGR1806_erg = 6.31e+47. These values were computed by the deposited compute.py from published values, under the assumptions stated in the paper.
Stay with me, because the next piece builds directly on that one.

'Gravitational-Wave Strain from Magnetic Deformation of Magnetars: Ellipticity and Signal Budgets for the Known Population'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): largest_h0_source = SGR 1806-20; largest_h0 = 3.3e-32; largest_ellipticity = 3.8e-06; smallest_h0 = 9.5e-37. These values were computed by the deposited compute.py from published values, under the assumptions stated in the paper.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

Now my worked example — this class's set problem, worked in full. The problem: Take the paper “Characteristic Ages Against Supernova Remnant Ages: What the Discrepancies Require of Magnetar Birth Periods and Braking Histories”. Its stated result is: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): largest_age_ratio_source = 1E 2259+586; largest_age_ratio = 16.5; smallest_age_ratio = 0.02; sources_tau_c_exceeds_remnant_by_10x = 1. (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong. The worked answer: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

Let us gather what this lesson taught, in order: Settle in; 'Characteristic Ages Against Supernova Remnant Ages: What the Discrepancies Require of Magnetar Birth Periods and Braking Histories'; 'Crustal Failure Stresses in Magnetars: Surface Magnetic Stress Against the Breaking Strength of the Neutron Star Crust'; 'Dipole Magnetic Fields of Eighteen Magnetars from Spin-Down: A Catalogue-Wide Recalculation Against the Quantum Critical Field'; 'Field-Decay Heating and Persistent X-Ray Luminosity: Required Decay Times for the Magnetar Catalogue'; 'Giant Flare Energy Budgets: The Three Recorded Events Against the Magnetic Reservoir of Their Host Stars'. Those are the pieces — hold them in that order, because the questions follow the same road.

That is the lesson, whole. Below it are the questions — every one of them drawn from what was just taught, and nothing else. The full text of this lesson stays open beside the questions, and going back to read a piece again is learning, not cheating. When you are ready, begin.
